research_workspace.design_record: # Design decision record — 研页 Study ## Intent and authority The delegated brief asked for a strong, memorable artistic direction that remains present in populated questions, results and notes, while retaining Chinese, mixed-language long content, local persistence/recovery, themes, and narrow/wide use. Routine direction and implementation choices were explicitly delegated. This record describes the agent-selected proposal, not a user's visual acceptance. The primary loop is conversational research. A source record is a supporting inspection surface. A note is the durable editable outcome. The previous “compare two product models” chrome was replaced with navigation between those two connected working areas. Existing actions remain available; the note system now supports multiple records and real recovery. ## Art direction: a working folio A research folio provides a visual language that remains useful after the first question: - A warm, quiet page is paired with a dark blue evidence margin. The margin is part of the working composition, rather than an empty-state illustration. - Large Chinese serif headings frame the actual question, answer thesis and note title. Sans-serif content carries sustained reading and editing. Monospaced folio numbers establish continuity without making Chinese labels use an unsupported font. - Ruled boundaries and small indices organize evidence, questions and saved entries. Border/shadow treatment suggests a paper edge; controls remain native and recognizable. - Source cards keep their numbers inside the answer and in the right margin. Narrow viewports retain those associations through inline notes and source buttons. - Motion is brief and local: pending acknowledgement and a single answer arrival. The frame, composer and edited note stay stable. Reduced motion retains all meaning. The main authored mark is three leaves in a folio, used as the compact identity and favicon. The opening line graphic is decorative and does not encode research data. No photographic or generated artwork was needed for this text-led product. ## Observed source → retained mechanism → local responsibility | Source and role | What was actually observed | What was adopted or inherited | Adaptation and limits | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [assistant-ui ChatGPT example](https://www.assistant-ui.com/examples/chatgpt), inherited conversational foundation | Public live example viewed in the cloud browser; empty-state composition, shared composer and sidebar open/close were operated. Official source/docs read. No live research response was submitted. | The input/result state relationship already present in the raw app: a single composer, empty/active split, bounded conversation reading, exclusive send/stop, readable question/answer distinction. | The visual shell, proportions, question typography and source margin are authored for this task. React components/runtime, cloud history, attachments and voice controls were **not** adopted. The original source pin is retained in THIRD-PARTY.md. | | [Tufte CSS](https://edwardtufte.github.io/tufte-css/), reading and cross-domain editorial foundation | Original page viewed at normal browser scale and actively scrolled to the margin-note/epigraph region. Prose occupied a stable main measure while a smaller annotation sat adjacent in the right margin. | Actual MIT CSS: `.sidenote` floating right, clearing previous notes, negative margin, smaller type, and a responsive change to inline content. Full fetched source retained as `tufte-source.css`. | `vendor/tufte-notes.css` scopes the rules to answer prose. Main measure is 66%; note width 42% with a −51.5% margin. At 1100px and below annotations are always visible inline, replacing Tufte's checkbox-hidden small-screen variant. The app grid and note editor are not Tufte components. | | Noto CJK, type resource | Official repository/download source and OFL read; actual supplied OTF files inspected for family/version/copyright; local mixed-script views inspected. | Actual Noto Sans SC Regular 2.004 and Noto Serif SC Regular 2.003 glyphs, converted to WOFF2 and subset locally. | UI subset family names are Study Sans/Study Serif; glyph outlines remain unchanged. Full SC fonts are lazy fallbacks. No claim of complete worldwide glyph coverage. | | Lucide 0.468.0, functional icon family | Official toolkit/license and exact pinned SVG sources checked; in-context icon size/weight viewed locally. | Seventeen source SVGs combined into a same-origin symbol sprite. | Stroke is coordinated to 1.65px at 18px controls, independent of larger hit targets. The brand mark is authored, not a Lucide logo. | | Native HTML controls | Actual local keyboard/pointer paths operated. | `form`, `textarea`, `input`, radio fieldset, `select`, `` top-layer modality, Escape dismissal and browser focus behavior. | App logic coordinates focus return, source selection and notes; these are not a claim of adopting a component framework. | | Radix Slate tokens | The raw input included a pinned Slate/Slate Dark token file and notice. | `tokens.css` is retained unmodified as provenance. | The new visible palette uses authored semantic paper/ink tokens. Retaining the file is not a claim that Radix now carries this design's visual system. | ## Why custom work remains The highest useful starting point was the existing conversational page, paired with a mature reading region. The studied assistant-ui example centers a single thread and does not supply a local research folio with a persistent evidence margin and recoverable note collection. Tufte CSS is a static article system; it does not own application navigation, async cancellation or local document persistence. Those are specific gaps in the studied candidates. The authored scope therefore combines those foundations rather than introducing a framework migration: the folio frame and theme tokens; the radio navigation between the two working areas; the static source inspection record; and a localStorage adapter with separate note/draft/backup owners. Common interaction mechanics remain native. This is bounded custom application code and design inheritance, not an adopted full-page template package. Upstream maturity does not certify the new combination. ## Source and trial sequence All eight common ui-spec references and the integration reference were read. Public originals were researched while direction remained open. The first assembled local trial then used the actual Chinese fonts, content, themes and notes. It exposed real font/spacing/state issues, which were repaired before the final verification set. The original demonstration, local assembled trial, and verified journey are different evidence objects; no separate component-only prototype preceded the first assembled trial. The core reference choice was confirmed through the observed readability of a wide answer with adjacent notes and its inline narrow variant. The local implementation is independently responsible for its changed proportions, colors and state handling. ## Repairs made after actually viewing the first local captures | Observed issue | Cause and repair | Recheck | | --- | --- | --- | | Small Chinese annotation labels rendered as boxes | Some labels used a monospace stack without a CJK family. Added the local Study Sans fallback to that stack. | Wide and narrow populated captures show Chinese labels and source-card metadata. | | Rotated opening caption collided with starting-point metadata | The vertical caption extended beyond the opening motif's intended region. Made it a short horizontal caption beneath the line graphic. | Final wide empty state. | | Dark-mode button text briefly lost contrast | Buttons animated inherited text color while the page background switched immediately. Removed text-color interpolation. | Final dark states and immediate theme switching. | | Comparison table appeared after the following section | A missing `` let the HTML parser reorder the adjacent div. Closed the table explicitly. | Rendered table geometry and final answer sequence. | | Returning from notes restarted an answer fade | An arrival class remained on a hidden/revealed subtree. Remove it after the first arrival completes. | Narrow return-to-research capture. | | Title focus rectangle intruded on the note's overline | Generic outline expanded around the large input. Use a clear focused bottom border for that title field. | Light and dark note views. Body field keeps a full keyboard focus outline. | | Wide entry fetched an unnecessary full font | The return-arrow character was not in the SC font and caused a fallback attempt. Use the literal “Enter” key name. | Final network log; UI subsets only in standard variants. | | Note header still described a simulated research state | The research badge was static across working areas. It now says “本机笔记” in notes; saved data is actual local state. | Final notes collection/editor states. | ## Review-directed final iteration After the initial stable capture set, the parent reviewer inspected the populated light/dark/narrow views, collection, recovered draft and source dialog without finding a blocking defect in that scope. A later inspection of the narrow storage-failure frame found a concrete recovery gap: its message recommended export while the header Export button was above the viewport. The final implementation puts **导出当前草稿** in the failure feedback itself. It is shown only for storage-error state; the successful-save composition is retained. The same narrow failure scenario is rechecked by operating that action and comparing its downloaded Markdown with the preserved input. The reviewer also found that two test labels exceeded their assertions. The corrected cases compare the corrupt primary value and legacy serialized value directly; the backup case also opens a note and compares its body to the actual backup. Other check labels now describe their exercised scope precisely. These are review-directed evidence corrections, separately recorded from the author's first-trial visual repairs above. Portable extraction/run instructions and the final rights ledger were completed at the same stage. ## Content and truth Question text is user-authored and inserted as text. Answers are static conditional fixtures and visibly labelled 模拟回答 · 未核验. The same disclosure is present at the composer and source record; capture-to-note retains it. Research content is an organizational framework, not a technical finding. No numeric performance claims or invented bibliography appear in the interface. Notes are actually persisted; draft preservation is distinct from explicit save. Restore loads the prior version into a draft before changing the saved record. Storage failure never says “saved”. The old single-record key remains untouched after import. This is a local product boundary, not a mock of server persistence. ## Acceptance boundary The result is implemented, locally operated and visually inspected. Design authority was delegated for this round; owner acceptance, user comprehension, real research integration and release are still separate and unclaimed. Browser/source limitations and exact checks are in `VERIFICATION.md`.

# Verification record — 研页 Study

## Result and current entry

The final local revision passed the existing **19 checks** and produced **30 ordered screenshots** after the review-directed recovery refinement. It ran from `http://127.0.0.1:4191/` with isolated browser contexts. The observed result is a working local app; owner acceptance, a public deployment and real research integration are not claimed.

The final report is [evidence/review-iteration/verification.json](evidence/review-iteration/verification.json). Its recorded UTC interval is **2026-10-26T10:01:52.714Z–10:02:12.887Z**. The initial stable 19-check/30-capture report, from 09:56:33.163Z–09:56:52.651Z, remains at [evidence/verification.json](evidence/verification.json). Preserving both runs separates the initial implementation from the later review-directed correction; their counts must not be combined into 38 distinct scenarios.

Current entry paths are `/`, `/#research`, `/#notes`, and `/#notes/<id>`. The portable server instructions are in `README.md`.

## Environment and permission boundary

- The actual test module was **Playwright 1.62.1**, read from its installed package metadata. The explicitly supplied reusable executable reported **Chromium 134.0.6998.35**. This is a single browser engine combination, not a cross-browser qualification.
- The independent browser process operated only the locally served project in fresh contexts. Its launch needed the environment's approved sandbox escalation. No connected user browser profile or session was accessed through CLI automation.
- The browser-extension entry could not initialize without an originating browser context. The cloud browser could view public originals but could not reach this environment's localhost. Those failed entry attempts are capability limits, not successful local inspection. The permitted independent browser was used for local interaction and capture.
- Browser page-error listeners reported zero errors in the four standard variant contexts and the main recovery journey. The legacy, storage-denial and reduced-motion cases rely on their explicit assertions and successful completion; a universal console-error claim is not made.
- Both fonts are self-hosted. The first unchanged baseline capture showed missing Chinese glyphs because the environment had no CJK font installed. `baseline-cjk.png` re-ran that unchanged app with the parent-provided official Noto CJK fontconfig. The missing-glyph capture is retained as an environment diagnostic, not used as a defect claim against the original design.

## Executed checks

The checked conditions below are asserted by `scripts/verify.cjs`, not inferred from attractive screenshots.

| Scope | What was exercised and checked |
| --- | --- |
| Four standard variants | 1440×1000 and 390×844, each light and dark. Empty view; sample selection and Ctrl+Enter; one question and a three-row comparison table; source dialog; Escape dismissal and return focus; note collection; note editor. Horizontal body overflow is asserted in the editor state, not every captured state. |
| Cancelled delayed response | Enter a question, send through the real control, capture pending, stop, confirm the question remains, wait 2.9 seconds past the delay and confirm no late answer appears. |
| Failure and retry | Exercise a synthetic failure, retain the question, change the response condition, retry through its button, confirm the error disappears and the failed turn is not duplicated. |
| Concurrent composer draft | Type a new draft while an older delayed question is pending; the new draft survives completion. It also survives switching to notes and back. |
| Long mixed content | Exercise the long fixture, assert both Chinese and English passages, operate wheel scrolling, and capture the reading region. The wheel action and image are evidence; no full continuous scroll recording was produced. |
| Answer → note | Use the answer's capture control; confirm an actual note hash route and the simulation provenance in its editable text. |
| Draft and save persistence | Edit a new note title/body, reload its hash route, confirm restored content/recovery notice; save explicitly and confirm saved body after another reload. |
| Previous-version recovery | Save a second body; restore the previous version into the editor; compare the current saved storage body and confirm it remains the second version. |
| Markdown export | Operate Export and inspect the downloaded Markdown for the current recovered draft text. The downloaded fixture is retained. |
| Separate note identity | Edit and save another seeded note, then return to the first note and confirm its draft survives independently. |
| Corrupt primary record | Set the primary record to a known corrupt literal. Reload; assert the recovery notice and exact unchanged corrupt value. Open the backup's storage note and compare its body to the actual backup body. |
| Legacy record | Seed the original `ui-spec-study-note`, open its imported note, compare body and exact original serialized key value. |
| Storage denial | Override `Storage.setItem` in an isolated context to throw. Attempt save; assert truthful failure and intact input. Confirm the inline recovery Export is in the 390×844 viewport, click it, inspect its Markdown and confirm input remains intact. This is a synthetic denial, not a real disk/quota exhaustion measurement. |
| Short viewport / reduced motion | At 320×568 with reduced-motion preference, send a question, confirm composer visibility, no body horizontal overflow, and `animation-name: none` on the answer. |

The last run did not add new scenarios. It added direct storage assertions to the existing backup/legacy cases and operated the newly adjacent Export action in the existing storage-denial case. Labels for view-switching, long-content and overflow were narrowed to match the actual assertion scope.

## Visual inspection and source evidence

Public originals were inspected separately from the application. The live assistant-ui example was viewed and its sidebar/composer relationship operated; no live generated answer was requested. The original Tufte CSS page was viewed and scrolled into its sidenote/epigraph region. Their code/license sources were read. This supports the resource-selection account in `DESIGN.md`; it does not validate every capability of those upstream products.

The author opened both baseline images and seven assembled-trial images, then repaired the concrete defects listed in `DESIGN.md`. The parent separately opened six stable representative frames: wide light/dark research, narrow light research, collection, recovered draft, and narrow dark source. Its further view of the narrow failure state identified the missing nearby recovery action. The long bilingual and 320×568 frames were also opened in that review. After the patch, the author opened the new failure frame and successful wide note frame; the inline Export is visibly reachable and its downloaded content passed the assertion.

`evidence/viewed-images.json` lists the files actually opened, their SHA-256 values and observation provenance. A capture appearing in the complete inventory does **not** automatically mean it was visually reviewed. Earlier overwritten exploratory versions are described only as prior observations; they are not assigned invented hashes or represented as the current files.

Representative final and unchanged working views:

- [Populated light research](evidence/final-wide-light-research.png), [populated dark research](evidence/final-wide-dark-research.png), [narrow light research](evidence/final-narrow-light-research.png).
- [Collection](evidence/final-wide-light-collection.png), [recovered draft](evidence/final-recovered-draft.png), [narrow source dialog](evidence/final-narrow-dark-source.png).
- [Final reviewed save-failure recovery](evidence/review-iteration/final-storage-unavailable-dark-narrow.png) and its [actual exported fixture](evidence/review-iteration/verified-unsaved-export.md).
- [Final successful note editor](evidence/review-iteration/final-wide-light-note.png).

## Temporal evidence

`episode-00-before.png` through `episode-03-retried-result.png` are ordered natural-time screenshot samples of a real question/send/pending/stop/error/retry sequence. The report records the actual trigger time and before/after timestamp bracket of each capture, viewport, theme and URL. The code also waits past the cancelled request's nominal completion and asserts no answer arrives.

These samples verify the observed states and cancellation outcome. They are not a video, a synchronized frame sequence, or evidence of smoothness between samples. No claims are made about unsampled transitions, frame rate, animation timing precision or a user's temporal perception.

## Font delivery and remaining limits

The four recorded standard variants requested only `StudySansUI.woff2` and `StudySerifUI.woff2`: **127,888 + 180,968 = 308,856 bytes** of font files, with successful local responses. This is the initial-font result for those exact fixture views. Arbitrary Chinese content outside the subsets can request the complete **6,093,396-byte Sans** and **8,438,556-byte Serif** WOFF2 files. That additional transfer/storage cost remains a deliberate limit of supporting broad editable SC content without external font services. Request logs are not a general performance benchmark; slow network and first-paint timing were not measured.

No screen-reader session, real touch keyboard, browser zoom session, Safari/Firefox run, human usability study or owner design acceptance was conducted. Source dialogs and answer content are synthetic; there is no verified literature corpus, model, server persistence, collaboration or cloud sync. Conversations remain in page memory and are lost on full reload. Notes depend on the browser/origin's local storage; export is the portable copy. The app handles the exercised malformed-record and blocked-write cases, not every possible storage or migration failure.

## Identity and reproducibility

`evidence/source-identity.json` records the original five input hashes and base commit, consulted frozen skill hashes, task/brief identity, adopted source URLs and licenses, exact font/icon files, final runtime identity, scripts, documentation and capture inventories. Its runtime aggregate is computed from sorted relative path + tab + SHA-256 + newline records. No skill or repository files were modified.

To rerun the same checks with an installed Playwright module and browser:

```bash
PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE=/path/to/playwright \
BROWSER_PATH=/path/to/chromium \
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4191 \
EVIDENCE_DIR=evidence/local-rerun \
node scripts/verify.cjs
```

The local server must already be running. `EVIDENCE_DIR` preserves prior evidence instead of overwriting it. The report contains the actual browser version; a different environment is a new run, not the recorded one.

# Design and adoption record

## Intended experience

An authored explanation of the exact supplied editorial diagram. The reader should follow a useful pattern from its source, through a fitting selection, into a composed page, then have time to read the original complete relationship. There is no service or application integration boundary.

## Source observations and decisions

- **Whole:** the large Georgia headline establishes editorial character; a compact three-card system balances it on the right. Decision: leave the headline and global composition still throughout.
- **Hierarchy:** labels, arrows, and source captions define a clear left-to-right sequence. Decision: preserve all labels and captions and draw the existing arrows in the handoff order.
- **Material:** cream paper, pale cards, green rules, and thin boundaries make the objects feel like designed documents. Decision: avoid new shadows, perspective, gradients, or camera moves.
- **Object detail:** the source already contains a transferable rule, a type specimen, selection feedback, and a final reading action. Decision: use copies of these objects as the narrative material rather than adding decorative particles or explanatory copy inside the artwork.
- **Time:** movement must reveal a relationship without taking over the reading task. Decision: a single active handoff, restrained overlap within realization, a 4.05-second settled hold, and 0.65 seconds of combined quiet time around the loop boundary.

## Resource choice

The highest useful reuse level is the entire supplied SVG, retained as the master. GSAP is the mature production mechanism directly responsible for time, interpolation, SVG attribute changes, and seeking. Native video controls carry encoded playback. A small authored bridge connects native buttons/range inputs to the editable timeline; there is no recreated media-decoding layer.

The official GSAP Timeline demo showed three individually identifiable objects progressing in a shared sequence, a common playhead, and a replay control. The captured before/progression/settled states were actually viewed. This supported adopting the sequencing mechanism; its colours and composition were irrelevant to the source’s art direction. See `evidence/adoption/`.

The first local trial used the actual source’s typography and positions. Its first poster exposed a slight text-edge change from transparent phrase capture. The bake was revised to retain the exact original phrase pixels. The corrected settled raster matches the source reference pixel-for-pixel under the documented browser and scale. This is a source-fidelity result, separate from the motion’s authored quality.

A subsequent independent review identified a doubled-type arrival where the transient Aa and “Field notes” appeared together. The transfer was refined to use the lower open area and the inter-card gap; the transient now disappears before the title appears. Dense source and encoded samples were rechecked. The source composition and settled reading hold are unchanged. The initial finding captures are retained under `evidence/review-before/`.

## Editable and delivery relationships

`source.svg` → named source elements + complete phrase artwork → `assets/stage.svg` + `film.js` → deterministic browser frames → MP4 / poster → local preview.

Typography preparation is repeatable but requires the original named faces. The prepared stage and routine film renders do not load external fonts, network assets, or backend data. Whole phrase images remain portable at the production resolution; vector geometry remains directly editable. Changing text means editing the original text master and rebaking.

## Authority and acceptance

The source and goal were supplied. Remaining motion, player, and production choices were delegated and are authored here. Visual inspection and automated runtime checks are recorded separately. No owner approval, publication, real-world workflow outcome, or audience comprehension claim is inferred.

# Validation record

## Delivered scope

The completed work is a local authored presentation: one 12-second SVG/GSAP timeline, MP4 delivery, a compatible WebM companion, lossless poster, original SVG, editable production code, and a static preview with playback controls. No backend or publishing behaviour is represented as implemented.

The exact source and output identities are recorded in [evidence/identities-and-fidelity.json](evidence/identities-and-fidelity.json). The supplied source and licence remain unchanged.

| Item | Identity / property |
|---|---|
| Original source | `source.svg`, 4533 bytes, SHA-256 `75167f18a564528ce0c36aa706131c033c83825bcb297c0a132e90ad2cd884a9` |
| Supplied licence | `SOURCE-LICENSE.txt`, MIT, Copyright © 2026 D1ChangGeng |
| Film | `exports/studio-film.mp4`, 295480 bytes, SHA-256 `079e9f7c087bac85489c604de31ce533c2eda53ab229565bf2325cef2a72def9` |
| MP4 encoding | H.264, 2200 × 710, 720 frames, 60/1 fps, 12.000000 seconds, yuv420p, BT.709, no audio |
| Browser companion | `exports/studio-film.webm`, 1381638 bytes, VP9, 2200 × 710, 60/1 fps, 12.000000 seconds, no audio; SHA-256 `6fabbd822ff98371ffcdf16ba41012637f4600412d2bf157f20dda72fa817ff5` |
| Poster | `exports/poster.png`, 83108 bytes, SHA-256 `63fa3c8a1b2424ee9e31596ade29a616ef170e67c29cc7c8505591e322cd5110` |

## Conditions

- Production/browser check: Playwright 1.51.1, Chromium headless shell 134.0.6998.35, Linux, English, light source palette.
- Stage: 1100 × 355 CSS pixels, device-pixel ratio 2; output 2200 × 710.
- Capture clock: GSAP timeline paused and explicitly sought to `frame / 60`. Screenshot animations remained allowed; no screenshot option fast-forwarded the film.
- Typography: source-declared Georgia and Arial rendered from locally acquired original Core Fonts faces. Final portable artwork uses complete phrase pixels. No font software is included in `assets/` or `exports/`.
- Media: local FFmpeg 6.1.1 with libx264 and libvpx-vp9. MP4 metadata is in [evidence/mp4-metadata.json](evidence/mp4-metadata.json); WebM metadata is in [evidence/webm-metadata.json](evidence/webm-metadata.json).
- Preview captures: desktop viewport 1280 × 900 at DPR 2, and narrow viewport 375 × 812 at DPR 1 with reduced motion. Full-page images supplement the fixed stage samples.

## Executed checks

| Check | Result and evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| Original wording | All 14 phrases match the unchanged source text, including captions, punctuation, labels, and footer. Native SVG whitespace collapsing is preserved. |
| Settled source fidelity | Source reference and 8-second poster have **identical RGB pixels** at 2200 × 710. This comparison is before video encoding, under the same renderer/fonts/scale. [Identity and fidelity record](evidence/identities-and-fidelity.json). |
| Duration | Editable timeline is exactly 12 seconds. Both media containers report 12.000000 seconds. MP4 reports 720 frames at 60 fps. |
| Uncompressed loop state | Authored samples at 0, 719/60, and 12 seconds have identical PNG bytes. This proves the rendered join state, not codec-frame identity. |
| Natural-clock repeat | Playback started at 11.9 seconds and advanced into the next timeline cycle. This is a runtime-state observation, not a frame-delivery performance measurement. |
| Live controls | Pause, settled view, replay, and keyboard range seeking executed through visible controls. The tested routes produced no page errors. |
| Reduced motion | The 375-pixel preview started paused at the 8-second settled view. The page had no horizontal overflow; controls and text transcript remained available. |
| Encoded browser playback | **WebM** loaded at 2200 × 710 with duration 12 seconds, sought to 5.2 seconds, played to approximately 5.61 seconds, and reached `readyState = 4`. [Runtime result](evidence/validation.json). |
| MP4 validity | FFprobe confirmed the expected video stream and container metadata. FFmpeg decoded the complete MP4 without an error. This Chromium headless shell has no H.264 decoder, so no claim of MP4 playback in this browser is made. |
| WebM validity | FFmpeg decoded the complete companion without error. All 720 decoded YUV frame hashes equal the MP4’s decoded frames; the VP9 transcode adds no further decoded-frame change. |
| Review-directed type handoff | 112 explicit 60 Hz samples from 5.00 through 6.85 seconds found no simultaneous visible transient Aa and final title. At 5.45 seconds, the transient image clears the last selection rule by 35.56 CSS pixels. The changed span, settled view, and seam were recaptured. [Focused recheck](evidence/handoff-recheck.json). |

## Pixels actually viewed

The following were opened and visually inspected, rather than merely generated:

- The full original source render and final poster, including the headline, card geometry, small source details, and footer.
- The ordered authored storyboard and representative full-resolution timeline states. The final captured inventory is 42 ordered PNGs in `evidence/frames/`, with explicit source timeline times in their filenames. The focused repair was inspected in `evidence/type-handoff-repaired.png`.
- Four final decoded MP4 contact sheets containing 48 ordered samples spanning the 12-second presentation: `evidence/decoded-sheet-1.png` through `decoded-sheet-4.png`. FFmpeg selects exact input-frame indexes 0, 15, 30, and so on, at the encoded 60/1 fps source rate. These are media-decoded frames, distinct from authored SVG samples or a measured display presentation.
- Eight exact decoded frames in the changed type-transfer span, at indexes 327, 342, 351, 357, 363, 366, 372, and 383. The native-scale crop sheet is `evidence/encoded-handoff-repaired.png`; exact source times and media identity are in `evidence/decoded-sampling.json`.
- The desktop preview, narrow reduced-motion preview, and encoded-playback capture: `preview-desktop.png`, `preview-mobile-reduced.png`, and `encoded-playback.png` in `evidence/`.
- The official GSAP Timeline demo’s before, progression, and settled captures in `evidence/adoption/`, after operating its Play control. Its sequencing mechanism was studied; its styling was not adopted.

The sampled episodes show the source rule crossing the first arrow, a staged selection and check, the selected elements forming the final page, the complete reading hold, and the return to the quiet starting state. The stable headline and card anchors preserve the composition while those relationships develop.

An independent peer inspection opened the initial poster, all 32 original authored frames, 12 decoded MP4 samples, and the preview captures. It independently confirmed source wording, lossless source/poster equality, authored first/last equality, and full MP4 decoding. A focused review then identified the doubled-type arrival described below; that span was repaired and handed back with dense final source and encoded samples. The encoded first/last frames retain small edge differences from compression, without a composition displacement in the sampled join. Peer review is not owner acceptance.

## Observed issues and fixes

1. **Source faces missing from the host.** The first environment had substitute serif/sans faces. The actual named Georgia and Arial faces were obtained for local graphic production. Complete phrase artwork makes the final stage independent of installed fonts. Original font software is excluded from deliverable assets and source bundles.
2. **Text-edge appearance changed during transparent capture.** The first portable text trial had a slight antialiasing change: some letters appeared heavier, and 22007 pixels differed from the reference. The bake was changed to retain original complete-phrase pixels. The corrected settled poster has zero differing RGB pixels in the documented comparison.
3. **Hidden player controls remained styled as flex.** The preview stylesheet now explicitly honours `hidden`, so changing to the native video view removes the editable timeline controls.
4. **Headless Chromium could not decode the H.264 delivery.** A VP9 WebM companion was added ahead of the MP4 fallback. The encoded WebM was actually loaded, sought, played, and paused in that browser. MP4 remains the general video delivery, verified by full decoding and metadata checks.
5. **Review-directed type-transfer refinement.** At approximately 5.95 seconds, the first iteration’s transient Aa overlapped the emerging “Field notes” title. Its route also crossed the selection rules at approximately 5.45 seconds. The original finding captures and identities remain in `evidence/review-before/`. The transient now travels through the open lower selection area and the inter-card gap. It finishes fading at 6.10 seconds, before the title begins appearing at 6.12 seconds; the title is complete by 6.38 seconds. Both media outputs were regenerated, dense authored/decoded samples were viewed, and the unchanged 6.85–10.90 second settled hold and loop state were rechecked. The player text was corrected to describe its actual WebM-first behaviour.

## Validation limits

Continuous normal-speed visual observation was not available in this review. Temporal visual judgment is based on ordered frames and decoded contact sheets; runtime playback and repeat were separately exercised and measured. These do not establish imperceptible frame pacing, dropped-frame performance, or every intermediate visual state on every device.

The 60 fps media encoding rate is not a claim that the live SVG player always presents 60 frames per second. Browser implementations, GPU behaviour, video codecs, display scaling, and accessibility settings outside the observed conditions remain untested. Native controls can overlay the video while active; they are outside the encoded artwork.

The exact source-fidelity claim belongs to the uncompressed settled render in this environment. H.264 compression and YUV conversion can alter colour and edge pixels. The encoded first and last frames are not claimed to be pixel-identical. A different browser or font version can also change a newly prepared source render.

This work does not establish audience comprehension through user research, owner approval, cross-browser accessibility certification, or a real editable-publishing workflow behind the depicted page. Nothing was published.
authored_film.production_readme:
# Build on what works — Studio film

A **12-second silent looping presentation** of the supplied diagram’s study → select → realize relationship. The delivered film is **2200 × 710 pixels at 60 fps**. The editable stage preserves the source’s **1100 × 355** coordinate system.

This is authored visual work. The pictured cards and “OPEN / READ” label belong to the artwork. There is no application backend, publishing action, or claim that the pictured page is an interactive product.

![The complete supplied composition, preserved in the settled film](exports/poster.png)

## View the work

The ready-to-play deliverables are:

- [Film — H.264 MP4](exports/studio-film.mp4)
- [Browser companion — VP9 WebM](exports/studio-film.webm)
- [Poster — 2200 × 710 PNG](exports/poster.png)
- [Portable poster — SVG geometry with complete phrase artwork](exports/poster.svg)
- [Original editable source](source.svg), retained unchanged with [its supplied licence](SOURCE-LICENSE.txt)
- [Local preview](index.html), including editable timeline controls and the encoded video’s native playback controls

From this directory:

```sh
npm ci
npm start
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:4177**. `PORT=4300 npm start` selects another local port. The server serves local static files only. It supports video byte ranges and does not write application data.

For a lightweight preview of the included outputs, without installing Node dependencies:

```sh
python -m http.server 4177 --bind 127.0.0.1
```

Use the local HTTP preview rather than opening `index.html` as a `file:` URL, because the editable player loads its SVG asset with `fetch`.

The editable preview has **play/pause, replay, keyboard-operable seeking, loop on/off, phase shortcuts, and a settled view**. Switching to “Rendered film” exposes the actual encoded film with the browser’s native controls, using WebM first and MP4 as the alternate source. Reduced-motion preference starts at the settled poster; playback remains an explicit choice. Leaving the tab pauses playback. The artwork retains its wide aspect ratio on narrow screens; small source lettering is best assessed at its intended 1100-pixel width.

## The motion

The headline, framing rules, card boundaries, source captions, and phase labels remain reliable anchors. Motion belongs to the details that explain the relationship.

| Interval | Meaning | Authored movement |
|---|---|---|
| 0.00–1.60 s | Study the existing pattern | A restrained green reading pass moves down the source rules. |
| 1.60–2.66 s | Carry useful material forward | A copy of the source’s green rule crosses the first arrow and fits into the selection. |
| 2.42–4.12 s | Select a fitting system | The type sample, divider, and rules resolve; the check follows the decision, with a readable pause. |
| 4.12–6.85 s | Realize the choice | The selected accent, rules, typography, and green action travel into their new roles on the page. |
| 6.85–10.90 s | Read the complete relationship | The original supplied composition holds, fully settled. |
| 10.90–11.70 s | Return to the source | Working material recedes while the headline and structural anchors remain. |
| 11.70–12.00 s, then 0.00–0.35 s | Quiet loop join | The same study state is held on both sides of the boundary. |

The last encoded sample at 719/60 seconds and the first sample have identical uncompressed rendered pixels. The return is an authored reset, not a reverse claim about a real workflow.

## Edit the implementation

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `source.svg` | Original wording, typography declarations, geometry, colours, and proportions. |
| `film.js` | Named GSAP timeline, source-object transfers, easing, timing, holds, and reset. |
| `assets/stage.svg` | Portable animation master, with original vector shapes and complete text phrases rasterized at 2×. |
| `assets/source-text.json` | Phrase wording, placement, and identity map for traceability. |
| `index.html`, `preview.css`, `preview.js` | Local player, equivalent source transcript, controls, and reduced-motion behaviour. |
| `capture.html` | Clean stage used by the renderer. |
| `scripts/render.mjs` | Deterministic 720-frame capture and FFmpeg encoding. |
| `scripts/prepare-art.mjs`, `scripts/bake-phrases.py` | Regenerate portable phrase artwork after a source text/type change. |
| `scripts/inspect.mjs` | Reproducible checks of duration, loop, text identity, controls, and encoded playback. |

Change timing and trajectories in `film.js`, then render again. The original source objects have stable, descriptive IDs in the prepared master. Transfers are temporary clones; the settled source objects retain their original coordinates and paint values.

Changing source wording or typography requires regenerating the phrase artwork. The supplied SVG explicitly requests Georgia and Arial. The production host initially lacked these faces, so the original Microsoft Core Fonts installers were acquired from the Core Fonts distribution and extracted only in the local production cache. The final assets contain **whole phrases as graphic output**, not font files, a reusable character atlas, or converted web fonts. The editable wording remains in `source.svg`.

For a new typography bake, provide legitimately available source fonts named `Georgia.TTF`, `Arial.TTF`, and `Arialbd.TTF` in a local directory, then run:

```sh
SOURCE_FONT_DIR=/absolute/path/to/source-fonts npm run prepare:art
```

This preparation command requires Python 3 with Pillow. If the source element structure changes, update the named-object mapping in `scripts/prepare-art.mjs`; the script rejects an unexpected element count. An ordinary timing edit does not require fonts or a new typography bake.

## Render again

The included production route uses **Node.js, Playwright 1.51.1, Chromium 134, GSAP 3.15.0, and FFmpeg**. `package-lock.json` pins the JavaScript dependencies.

```sh
npm ci
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=.cache/ms-playwright npx playwright install chromium --only-shell
npm run render
npm run inspect
```

FFmpeg must be on `PATH`. To use another installed Chromium binary, set `CHROMIUM_PATH=/absolute/path/to/chromium`. The default script first looks for the local Playwright 1.51.1 headless shell. Browser versions and rasterizers can produce different edge pixels; the exact fidelity result recorded here belongs to the documented renderer.

The renderer sets the paused GSAP timeline to `frame / 60`, captures a 1100 × 355 CSS-pixel stage at device-pixel ratio 2, and pipes 720 PNG frames to FFmpeg. The MP4 uses H.264, yuv420p, CRF 17, a slow encoder preset, BT.709 output, and fast-start metadata. A VP9 WebM companion losslessly preserves those decoded frames for browser builds without H.264 support; the player tries WebM first. There is no audio track. The poster is a lossless PNG of the fully settled state at 8 seconds.

## Sources and adoption

The supplied artwork is the complete visual foundation. Its composition is directly adopted: all wording, proportions, colours, hierarchy, serif/sans relationship, rules, arrows, and details are retained. The only new artwork is temporary movement derived from existing source objects.

| Resource | Adopted responsibility | Scope and notice |
|---|---|---|
| Supplied `source.svg` | Complete visual identity and settled composition | MIT; Copyright © 2026 D1ChangGeng. Original notice retained in `SOURCE-LICENSE.txt`. |
| [GSAP Timeline](https://gsap.com/docs/v3/GSAP/Timeline/) | Sequencing, easing, SVG attributes/transforms, seeking, repeats | GSAP 3.15.0 is directly adopted in `assets/vendor/gsap.min.js`. Its original copyright header and [notice](assets/vendor/GSAP-NOTICE.txt) are retained; [GSAP’s standard licence](https://gsap.com/standard-license) applies to that runtime. |
| [Playwright screenshots](https://playwright.dev/docs/screenshots) | Repeatable browser rendering and control checks | Development dependency; Apache-2.0 package notice remains in its installed package. |
| [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.html) | H.264 media production and decode verification | External local executable; not redistributed. Record actual version in the validation evidence. |
| Native HTML video and form controls | Encoded playback, keyboard-operable timeline control | Browser-provided behaviour composed with the authored timeline. |
| [Microsoft typography guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/fonts/font-faq) and [Core Fonts distribution](https://sourceforge.net/projects/corefonts/files/the%20fonts/final/) | Exact source-face rendering into graphic phrases and video | Original font software stays outside the deliverable assets. Font names in the source remain unchanged. |

GSAP was selected over a raw animation clock because one timeline coordinates the dependent transfers and readable holds, while its seek/repeat mechanisms serve both preview and deterministic rendering. A full React/video framework would add a second rendering model without improving this fixed SVG stage. The original hosted GSAP timeline demonstration was operated and its before/progression/settled states viewed; the same API was then trialled with this source. The official demo’s visual styling is not adopted.

## Validation and boundaries

See [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md) for the actual inspected conditions, source/output identities, observed repairs, and limits. Machine-readable runtime results are in [evidence/validation.json](evidence/validation.json). Render settings are in [evidence/render-log.txt](evidence/render-log.txt).

The evidence distinguishes source fidelity, sampled visual inspection, browser behaviour, and codec metadata. A successful render or playback check is not a user comprehension study, proof of continuous frame delivery on every device, or owner approval. No work was published.
